connections.title: Marriage of Meir Yehuda Feldman and Chaya Feige

enrichment.markdown:
**Meir Yehuda Feldman**

- The Drohitchin memorial text expands his family considerably: his parents were **Michael Feldman** and **Heska**; his wife, **Chaya Feiga**, was the daughter of **Yaakov Hersh and Pesha Kaminetsky**. The couple had children including **Leiba, Bashka, Yosef, Avraham Mordechai, Heska**, and **Esther Beila**. ([JewishGen, pp. 223–224](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro223.html); [JewishGen, pp. 410–411](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro410.html))

- He emigrated to the United States in **1892**, living for four years in **St. Joseph, Missouri**, where he helped establish the **Sha’arei Shalom synagogue**. He later returned to Drohitchin. ([JewishGen, pp. 223–224](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro223.html))

- From **1897 until 1914**, he leased and managed the **Smolnik Estate**, owned by Count Kontorov. The Czarist authorities forced the family to leave the estate in 1914 under residential restrictions. ([JewishGen, pp. 223–224](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro223.html))

- The evidence is inconsistent on his final fate. One account says that Meir Yehuda and Chaya Feiga “died with their family” in Drohitchin; another wartime testimony places **Meir Yudel** among Jews outside the ghetto shortly before the town’s destruction. Neither passage supplies a precise death date or transport. ([JewishGen, p. 223](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro223.html); [JewishGen, p. 306](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro306.html))

**Children and descendants**

- **Heska Feldman**, later **Heska Match**, emigrated to the United States in **1922**, married **Shmuel Match** in Chicago in 1930, and had three children: **Sarah Leah, Yisrael Ezra, and Morry**. ([JewishGen, p. 410](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro410.html))

- **Esther Beila Feldman** was born in **1889**, married **David Friedman** in 1907, emigrated with her family, and died in **St. Joseph, Missouri, on September 25, 1954**. ([JewishGen, p. 410](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro410.html))

- **Avraham Mordechai Feldman**, born in Drohitchin in **1883**, arrived in the United States in **1904** and died in **Denver on April 2, 1956**. His widow was **Roza, née Baskov**; they had three children. ([JewishGen, p. 411](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro410.html))

- **Leiba Feldman**, identified as Meir Yudel’s son, was later held in a wartime labor camp. ([JewishGen, p. 302](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro302.html))

**Grassman family and Khomsk Lane**

- The connected Grassman names are clarified: **Gedaliah Grassman** died in Drohitchin in 1942; his sons included **Yirmiyahu**, deported by the Bolsheviks to Russia and later living in New York, **Chaim Leib Herman**, who lived in New York, and **Zelig**, who perished in Drohitchin. The “Grassman wall” stood beside **Khomsk Alley**. ([JewishGen, p. 223](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Drohichyn/dro223.html))

- I found no separate archival matches for **Jacob Hirsch**, **Fieshe**, or the exact street spelling “Khamsker Lane” in the searched JewishGen, Yad Vashem, USHMM, and Arolsen interfaces; “Khomsk Alley” is the corroborated variant.
